findings.explanation: The example passes runtime = "python37", which reached end of support in 2023 and has since been decommissioned: it receives no security patches and new deployments are rejected. The module accepts any runtime string, so nothing stops a caller copying this. No holden policy checks google_cloudfunctions_function.runtime.
findings.remediation: Use a supported runtime (python312) in the example, and validate var.lambda.runtime against known decommissioned runtimes in the module.
findings.resolution: Example runtime set to python312; var.lambda validation now rejects decommissioned runtimes.
findings.title: Example deploys the function on the decommissioned python37 runtime

findings.explanation: kms_key_name is mandatory in this module, but docker_repository is never set. Google requires a CMEK function (1st gen) to name an Artifact Registry repository encrypted with the same key; without it the deploy is rejected or the built image lands in the Google-managed gcf-artifacts repository outside the CMEK boundary. The engine only checks that kms_key_name is set (HLD_GCP_086), not its companion.
findings.remediation: Expose a docker_repository input, pass it to the function, and have the example create a CMEK-encrypted DOCKER repository and grant the Artifact Registry service agent the key.
findings.resolution: Added optional docker_repository input passed to the function; example creates a CMEK DOCKER Artifact Registry repo and grants the AR service agent the key.
findings.title: CMEK Cloud Function has no Artifact Registry docker_repository, so build images are not covered by the key

findings.explanation: GCS requires the CMEK key to be in the bucket's location and Cloud Functions requires it in the function's region. The module feeds the same var.kms_key_name to both, yet defaults the bucket location to the "eu" multi-region while functions run in a single region, so the default can never apply. The example repeats the mismatch: a us-central1 key ring encrypting two "eu" buckets. Apply-time failure, filed under reliability as the best fit.
findings.remediation: Default the bucket location to var.region (location = null falls back to region) and put the example's key ring and buckets in var.region.
findings.resolution: location now defaults to null and falls back to var.region; example key ring and buckets use var.region.
findings.title: One kms_key_name is used for the source bucket (default location "eu") and the function (region), which GCP cannot satisfy

findings.explanation: The object name is basename(var.sourcezippath). When the zip changes the object is replaced under the same name, so source_archive_object on the function does not change and Cloud Functions v1 keeps running the old code. Deploys look successful while shipping nothing.
findings.remediation: Include the archive's MD5 in the object name so a new zip changes source_archive_object and triggers a redeploy.
findings.resolution: Object name now includes filemd5 of the zip, so new code changes source_archive_object and redeploys.
findings.title: Source archive object name is static, so code changes never redeploy the function

findings.explanation: The lifecycle rule deletes any object older than 90 days, including the archive the function is deployed from, so any later update of the function fails until Terraform re-uploads it. Because versioning is on, the 'deleted' object becomes a noncurrent version that no rule ever removes, so the rule does not bound storage either. HLD_GCP_339 only checks that a lifecycle rule exists.
findings.remediation: Expire only noncurrent versions (days_since_noncurrent_time) instead of live objects.
findings.resolution: Lifecycle rule now deletes only noncurrent versions (days_since_noncurrent_time = 30).
findings.title: Code bucket lifecycle deletes the live source archive after 90 days and keeps noncurrent versions forever

findings.explanation: The CMEK function needs the gcf-admin-robot service agent to hold cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter before creation, but depends_on lists only the GCS grant, so the function can be created before its key grant exists (plus IAM propagation) and fail on first apply.
findings.remediation: Add google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.cloudfunction_encrypter_decrypter (and the Artifact Registry grant) to the module's depends_on.
findings.resolution: Example module depends_on now includes the Cloud Functions service agent key grant.
findings.title: Example module waits for the GCS key grant but not the Cloud Functions service agent key grant

findings.explanation: map(any) forces every value to one type, documents no keys and validates only that the map is non-empty. ingress_settings is read with try(..., default), so a misspelt key silently falls back to the default, and a missing required key only fails as an Invalid index deep in the resource.
findings.remediation: Type var.lambda as an object with the required attributes and optional() defaults, and move value validation (ingress_settings, timeout, runtime) into variables.tf.
findings.resolution: var.lambda is now a typed object with optional ingress_settings/retry and validations for ingress_settings, timeout, runtime and service_account_email. Callers passing the same keys are unaffected.
findings.title: var.lambda is an untyped map(any) read with try(), so typos and missing keys fail late or silently

findings.explanation: failure_policy.retry = false is fixed in the module, so any transient failure handling a storage or Pub/Sub event loses that event with no way for a caller to opt into retries.
findings.remediation: Make retry configurable through var.lambda (optional, default false to keep current behaviour).
findings.resolution: Added optional lambda.retry (default false, unchanged behaviour).
findings.title: Event trigger retry is hardcoded off, so failed events are dropped

findings.explanation: The bucket is always named "${var.project}-lambdacode-bucket". A second instance of the module in the same project collides on the globally unique bucket name.
findings.remediation: Add an optional bucket_name input that defaults to the current name, so existing deployments keep their bucket.
findings.resolution: Added optional bucket_name input defaulting to the existing name.
findings.title: Source bucket name is derived only from the project, so the module can be used once per project

findings.explanation: The comment describes a public grant, contradicting the invoker validation that rejects allUsers and allAuthenticatedUsers. Misleading for maintainers reviewing access.
findings.fix: # Grants roles/cloudfunctions.invoker to the single named principal in var.invoker
findings.remediation: Reword the comment to describe the single named invoker.
findings.title: Invoker IAM comment says 'all users' although the variable forbids allUsers

findings.explanation: HLD_PROPOSED_006 is the same check as built-in HLD_GCP_287 (max_instances >= 1) and triggers a placeholder-ID warning on every scan; .holden/proposed-policies/HLD_PROPOSED_007 duplicates built-in HLD_GCP_288. Both were adopted upstream and are now dead weight.
findings.remediation: Delete both files; the built-ins already enforce them.
findings.resolution: Deleted HLD_PROPOSED_006 and HLD_PROPOSED_007; built-ins HLD_GCP_287/288 cover them.
findings.title: Local holden policies duplicate built-in policies and carry placeholder IDs

suggested_policies.rationale: Decommissioned Cloud Functions runtimes get no security patches and can no longer be deployed; the runtime string is a single attribute with an unambiguous pass/fail and no built-in policy checks it.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: LOCAL_GCP_001
name: Cloud Functions must not use a decommissioned runtime
principle: patch-management
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  Decommissioned Cloud Functions runtimes (python37/38, nodejs6-16, go111-118,
  ruby26/27, php73/74, dotnet3) receive no security patches and Google rejects
  new deployments on them.
message: |
  The function uses a decommissioned runtime.
remediation: |
  Set runtime to a supported version, e.g. runtime = "python312".
resources:
  google_cloudfunctions_function:
    path: runtime
    not_matches: "^(python3[78]|nodejs(6|8|10|12|14|16)|go1(11|13|16|18)|ruby2[67]|php7[34]|dotnet3)$"

suggested_policies.rationale: A 1st gen Cloud Function with kms_key_name must also name a CMEK Artifact Registry docker_repository; the check is a single-resource conditional that applies to any Terraform using the type.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: LOCAL_GCP_002
name: CMEK Cloud Functions must set a docker_repository
principle: encryption
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  A Cloud Function (1st gen) encrypted with a customer-managed key must store its
  build image in an Artifact Registry repository encrypted with the same key.
  Without docker_repository the image is outside the CMEK boundary or the deploy fails.
message: |
  kms_key_name is set but docker_repository is not.
remediation: |
  Set docker_repository to a CMEK-encrypted Artifact Registry DOCKER repository.
resources:
  google_cloudfunctions_function:
    if_present:
      path: kms_key_name
      then:
        path: docker_repository
        not_null: true
